title: RiskClassification
description: The classification an agent (or a code guard) assigns to a pending action, determining whether it may proceed autonomously or must be gated. Produced before any state-changing action.

action.description: The pending action, concretely (the exact command, send, or write).

tier.description: 0 = trivial/local, fully reversible. 1 = easily reversible with minor effort. 2 = costly or annoying to reverse, still internal. 3 = destructive, outward-facing, financial, credential-touching, or effectively irreversible. See references/safety.md.

reversible.description: Can the effect be undone without external cost or notice?

outward_facing.description: Does the effect cross the trust boundary (send, publish, external write)?

money_moving.description: Does it move funds, change budgets, or incur charges?

credential_touching.description: Does it read, write, or transmit secrets or credentials?

blast_radius.description: Exact scope of effect, quantified where possible ('deletes 412 files', 'changes price on 3,412 SKUs', 'emails 18,904 recipients').

affected_entities.description: The specific records, files, accounts, or recipients affected.

requires_confirmation.description: True when tier exceeds the task's max_risk_tier. Drives the confirmation gate.

safer_alternative.description: A lower-tier way to achieve the same goal (archive vs. delete, --force-with-lease vs. --force, draft vs. send), if one exists.

evidence.description: The specific evidence that this action (not a pattern-matched cousin) is the right one. Enforces Principle 7.
